utterances.text: Well, Mr. Emmerson, when there is two dates; the first date closing of the post office, and one month later being called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll read the passages from the statement. The first one reads: "I was from March 1998 until I left Kosovo on the 15th or 16th of June, 1999, working in the police, so I was from March 1998 working in the police." And the second paragraph I referred to reads: "About mid-April, I was summoned to work as a police reservist." So I think it is clear that the witness in the statement was referring to two different dates for the same event.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you be sure now whether it was March or April or do you not really know?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, time means nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it -- could it be either date?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in April, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware of a major fire-fight that had been launched by Serb police forces in Gllogjan on the 24th of March in which a police officer called Otovic was killed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd heard of it, yes, and I knew that Otovic had been killed. I'm not sure about the date, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, if you take it from me that the date was the 24th of March, was it before or after that incident in Gllogjan that you were called up as a reservist?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: After that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you tell us roughly how long after that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to see if I've understood the answers you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could you please also explore the relation 24th of March and closing the post office and moving into --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know whether you stopped delivering as a postman before or after the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if I've understood it correctly, there was an interval, you told us, of about a month between you ceasing to deliver post and you being called up full time as a policeman. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, wouldn't it be more clear to the closure of the Streoc police -- post office when I think the witness said he moved to Decane and there had his --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I used the expression that I did, but it may be that it wasn't as clear as it might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, so that we're clear and in answer to the Judge's question, you told us that there was a date on which the post office in Strellc was closed and that you worked for a time after that from the post office in Decane. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was the interval between the two about a month, between the closure of the post office in Strellc and the time when you first began working full time as a police officer, was it about a month?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: About a month, 20 days, up to a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just specifically to deal then with the Judge's question, do you remember now whether the closure of the post office at Strellc happened before or after the incident in Gllogjan when the police officer called Otovic was killed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you asked -- you were asked and answered some questions by the Judge just before the break about the circumstances in which you came to be called up. And you said: It wasn't a choice, it was obligatory. You get assigned, and I think you said it was a war assignment. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, so that we're clear, could anybody be assigned, or did you have to have been on the register as a reserve police officer beforehand?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know there is a list of reserve policemen, and this is determined by the military post number or perhaps by the military police, either way. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question to you a slightly different way. Were many of your friends and relatives also drafted in to the police during 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll ask you a little bit about those in a few moments. You told us that you were armed with a pistol and an automatic weapon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think I'm right in saying that all reserve policemen who were called up were armed with pistols and automatic weapons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's not correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So why were you chosen to have a pistol and an automatic weapon, as far as you understood it, Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, you must have discussed it, surely, with your colleagues who weren't armed, you've told us. How did the decision come to be made about who had automatic weapons, who had pistols, and so forth?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you saying that there were reserve police officers who had no weapons at all?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I -- that's an ambiguous answer, I'm afraid. Can you answer me in this way: Is it your evidence that there were some reserve police officers who had no weapons? Are you saying some of them had no weapons at all?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry, you'll have to answer in a sentence, please. Can you please put it in your own words?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not know of any police officers with no weapons. There may have been some, but none that I knew of.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I thought you told us a little while ago that not everybody had automatic weapons. Is that right, not all the police officers in the reserve police had automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Some had semi-automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see, I see. And the AK-47, what is that, an automatic or a semi-automatic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Automatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that what you had?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But no idea why you were given one?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that you never used it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, please, the answer's ambiguous. Is it -- are you telling the Tribunal that you, yourself, never fired your automatic weapon at all at any time? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you used it, please?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in Kodralija when we came under fire. We were trying to pull out the bodies of four policemen from Novi Sad, and I used the weapon in self-defence on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you kill anybody?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Actually, when was that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that the only occasion on which you've discharged your automatic weapon?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I just ask one question? You mentioned the place which does not appear clearly on the transcript. Was it Kodralija or -- which I find on my map as being quite near to Pozar, or was it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Kodralija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that between Pozar and Rznic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that have been in 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever enter that area during 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I passed through, when we were on our way to look for Slobo and Milos.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that the only time you went into that area during 1998, Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What about your pistol, did you ever have occasion to use that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just put a general question to you for a moment, Mr. Markovic. You are aware, aren't you, that there was during 1998 fighting going on in various villages in western Kosovo between the Yugoslav Army and the police on the one hand, and armed Albanian groups on the other. You were aware that there was fighting going on in 1998 at various points?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Full-scale battles?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about full-scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, are you aware that there was a major Serbian offensive, for example, in the second half of May in the area of western Kosovo that you were living in?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what about the beginning of August when police forces over-ran Gllogjan and Irzniq and ousted the KLA, were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard of it, but I was not involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can I ask you, were you aware from all the conversations you'd overheard outside the police station that it was the policy of the police and particularly paramilitary units that after a village had been bombarded to go in and conduct mopping-up exercises, as they're described?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean "mopping-up"?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Burning people's houses, stealing their property, shooting their livestock, setting their haystacks on fire, and killing any civilians that remained behind, that sort of mopping-up. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever take --

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Not the -- about withdrawals.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't think I understood that answer. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: You asked me about withdrawals when they were withdrawing and then killing on their way. I never heard anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Did you ever take part in any such operations where you entered villages after they had been over-run by Serb military forces?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll come back to that, if we may. Your younger brother Rade, you told us he was a company manager. He was also in the reserve police, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you a passage from his witness statement, Mr. Markovic, because you're lying to this Tribunal now, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your brother Rade is about a year younger than you, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you both share the same father, whose name is Radovan, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me read to you a passage from a witness statement that he made and signed to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 10th of May, 2002. He says: "I am a high school graduate and attended two years of post-high school education at an economist's school. I did an obligatory year of service with the JNA in 1984 and 1985. I was a communications operator. I was a reserve police officer in Decane in 1991, and from 1997 until approximately four months before the OSCE came to Kosovo. My duties in 1998 were guarding the police station in Decane. I wore a blue uniform and was armed with an AK-47 automatic rifle. I was never involved in active operation against the KLA." So he was stationed, he says, outside Decane police station. What's your explanation, Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Between 1991 and 1997, he was occasionally with the reserve police forces. He guarded the station, just like I did, and then he contracted lung disease, some form of tuberculosis, and as result of his illness, in 1998, he definitely was not a member of the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, you gave me an unequivocal answer a few moments ago that he was not a reserve police officer. But leaving that aside, let me read you the passage again: "My duties in 1998 were guarding the police station in Decane. I wore a blue uniform and was armed with an AK-47 assault rifle," his duties in 1998, Mr. Markovic. Now, you're lying to the Tribunal about this, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The date of that statement was the 10th of May, 2002. Now, your statement to the Prosecution was also made on the 10th of May, 2002, Mr. Markovic. Do you remember being at the same building with your brother when the statements were made?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson -- Mr. Markovic, earlier Mr. Emmerson asked you whether your brother also was in the reserve police force. He said he was, wasn't he; and you said no. Now you say that during certain intervals he was. Why did you say no earlier on this question of Mr. Emmerson's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Mr. Emmerson asked his question, I was thinking about 1998 and 1999. My brother was a reserve policeman between 1991 and 1997, until he got ill; after that, he wasn't in the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, you made a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, and I'm emphasising the whole truth. If Mr. Emmerson asks you whether your brother was in the police force, then if he ever was, you should have told us that he was, although perhaps at another moment. May I invite you to be as complete as possible in your answers. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, can you think of any reason why your brother should tell the Prosecutor that he was working outside Decane police station with an AK-47 in 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that he was working in 1997, but I'm sure that he wasn't working in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As you've told us that you're not very good on dates, is there a possibility that you might be mistaken or are you saying that your brother must have said something to the Prosecutor that wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: He may have been in January or February 1998, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We're moving forwards a little now. He may have been in January or February 1998, but you can be categorically sure he wasn't in March. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No. What I want to say that we were not together in the reserve police, the two brothers were not there. When I was in the reserve police, he wasn't; that's what I wanted to say and that is why I'm sure that in 1998, when I was a reserve police officer, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course we don't really know when you started, do we? You don't know when you started, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It should have been sometime in April, towards the end of April. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Now, bearing in mind what the Judge has just told you about making sure that you don't give us inaccurate information while you're under oath, I'm going to ask you about some other people. And just so that it's fair to you, Mr. Markovic, we have records. Let me ask you about some other friends of yours. Slobodan Markovic, was he a police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see him with weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: He was working in Djakovica, not in Decani, and I suppose he had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, he wasn't a traffic police officer, for example, with white gloves during this period of the conflict, was he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that he was a traffic policeman in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you have traffic policemen while the roads were blocked, as you've described, and you had to drive along convoys? Were there traffic policemen at that point, generally?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the witness said: "I know he was a traffic policeman in 1997."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you are referring to a part of the testimony which is not in 1997?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm asking about 1998. During 1998 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it's confusing the way you put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: During 1998, were there traffic policemen with white gloves directing the traffic along the roads?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean directing the traffic at intersections?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So whatever he was in 1997, you certainly wouldn't have expected to see Slobodan Markovic directing the traffic in 1998, would you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. Is he related to you [Realtime transcript read in error missing word "you"], Slobodan Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is he your cousin?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Rade Vlahovic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He was a police officer, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was he in the regular or the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Regular.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you see him in Decane during 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Ljubisa Radunovic, this is the son of Milos Radunovic, whose body you were involved in the discovery of. Ljubisa Radunovic was an old friend of yours, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he was a police officer, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see him during 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I draw your attention to page 59, line 9. There "he" appears where it's not very clear to me to whom you referred when you said "is he" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I think the question, in fact, is mistranscribed. The question was: "Is he related to you, Slobodan Markovic?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then if that's understood and I take that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he replied: "Yes, he is." "Q. Is he your cousin?" "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, then, it's clear to me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Predrag Stojanovic, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: If they call him Dragan, yes, but Predrag Stojanovic, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Predrag and Dragan are the same person, according to the evidence that we have heard. You know Dragan Stojanovic, yes?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he was a police officer, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see him during 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No. You're asking me about the policemen who were working in Djakovica while I was in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And Veselin Stojanovic, he was a police officer, his brother, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Stanisa Radosevic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. When was Stanisa Radosevic called up to the police, or was he a permanent police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When was he mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, was he there at the same time as you in Decane? Because you've told us you saw him in Decane.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So is that yes, he was mobilised at the same time as you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Come on, Mr. Markovic. You've told us in your evidence already that you spoke to him in Decane, because it was a small place and you couldn't help running into people and talking to them, and he's a long-term friend of yours, isn't he? He lived next door to your grandfather. Was he in the reserve police at the same time as you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did it take you so long to answer a straight question, Mr. Markovic? MR. DI FAZIO: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I withdraw the question. I withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because if you look at the question "at the same time," it's not totally unambiguous what happened at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. The last question now was a bit different. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So he was mobilised at the same time as you. Does that mean that he was mobilised during April?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, it seems that the witness makes a distinction between serving at the same time and being mobilised --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at the start of entering, and that seems to create the confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you were called up, was he already a police officer in the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, roughly how long after you were called up can you tell us for sure that he was in the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I know for sure that he was in the police when we discovered his father's body.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So by the time you went to Dashinoc in September, he was already a police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I'm just going to ask you a question generally, Mr. Markovic, because Stanisa Radosevic has given evidence that he was never in the police or the reserve police. You have given evidence that your brother wasn't, despite the fact that he's made a statement that he was. I want to ask you: Is there somebody who told you that you shouldn't be telling the Tribunal the truth about who was in the police and who wasn't?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did -- you tell us about this Serbian man who came to visit you just before you were due to give evidence. Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: What Serbian are you asking me about? Nobody came to caution me or to talk to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise. I withdraw the question. I made a genuine mistake on my part? Do you know what the letters PJP stand for?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Special police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Some police officers were selected for this special police unit, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And could you be selected for the special police unit from the reserve police as well as from the full-time police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we please look at D14, please, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a list, Mr. Markovic, of officers who in March 1999 were being paid as members of the PJP? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm -- must have a faulty memory. I thought this was a creation of -- can the witness take off his --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He speaks English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He speaks English. MR. DI FAZIO: I thought it was a creation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one doesn't contradict the other. Let me just have a -- MR. DI FAZIO: I have no problems in Mr. Emmerson suggesting that these are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- I think this is a discussion we shouldn't have in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me ask the questions without describing what the list is. We -- all of us know what the list is -- MR. DI FAZIO: I have absolutely no quarrel with that. I understand perfectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put it differently then, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, the list of names in front of you are names that appear on lists of individuals who were in the pay of the PJP in March 1999. It's not a complete list, of course, but these names all appear in the records of the PJP. And if we just go down the list to see those you recognise. You've told us about Rade Vlahovic. Did you know that he was in the PJP?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What about Stanisa Radosevic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us that people -- you thought at least people couldn't join the PJP from the reserve police. Let's be clear, was Stanisa Radosevic in the reserve police or the full-time police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was a reserve police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Slobodan Markovic, your cousin, what about him?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. All these men are from Djakovica and I don't know about them. I only see Danilo Stijovic here on this list who is completely unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. The others are -- you know all of them, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Rade Vlahovic, yes; Stanisa Radosevic, yes; Zeljko Radosevic, I think so, Zeljko Radosevic, I think he is originally from Montenegro if that's the person I'm referring to but I'm not sure about him; Slobodan Markovic, my cousin; Momcilo Markovic, I don't know who that is; Predrag Stojanovic, if that's Dragan I know him; Veselin Stojanovic, I didn't even know that he was a policeman; Ljubisa Radunovic, I know him, but I don't know that they were members of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Of the people on that list, Mr. Markovic, one is your cousin and two are your childhood friends from Dashinoc, Stanisa Radosevic and Ljubisa Radunovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Rade Vlahovic is my first cousin, so a very close relative. Slobodan Markovic is a distant relative, and Stanisa Radosevic and Ljubisa Radunovic were my neighbours from the village, and Predrag Stojanovic I know through my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me ask you a little bit more generally about the period of March to April 1998. Now, you've told us that there was a time when two out of the three roads into Decane were blocked. Do you remember giving us that evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in your witness statement - and for those following, it's page 4, paragraph 5 - you said that those two roads were blocked during March. Is that correct or wrong?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I told you that timing didn't mean anything to me. I don't know whether it was in March or in April. I think April.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you also said in your statement, page 4, paragraph 5, that at the time that occurred, there were only 15 policemen in Decane. Was that the truth?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And then you and others were mobilised, and those numbers swelled to 130. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: 130 is way too much, around 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, again, I'm taking this from your own witness statement, page 5, paragraph 5, in which you said there were a hundred police officers stationed at the children's camp in Decane and 30 at the police station. Is that right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it would be 130 in Decane?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why did you tell us it was way too high?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you trying to paint a misleading picture to the Tribunal of the strength of the forces in Decane?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know there were internationals in the area from the 24th of March onwards?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you - and I'm putting this to you from a report filed by the British military attache to Belgrade who was in Decane on the 24th of March - that there were between 8 to 10.000 MUP officers in western Kosovo, including 5 to 700 members of the PJP in March 1998. Can I ask your reaction to that, please?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put something else to you, Mr. Markovic. The same gentleman has filed a statement in which he says that the PJP were supported by - and I'm quoting him - "imported thugs who were brought in to stir up trouble so that the MUP could step in and sort out the participants." Can you think who he might be referring to "as imported thugs who were brought in to stir up trouble" in March 1998 in the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know who General Bozidar Delic is?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him at the Milosevic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You were following that on the screen, were you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you know that he was at the time, in March, a colonel commanding the 549th Brigade in the area where you were a police officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No -- what's not correct about it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that he was a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You knew --

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: And I didn't know him then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us you followed his evidence in the Milosevic trial. You knew he was the commander of the Yugoslav Army then in the area where you were a police officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you what you do know about it since you were following his evidence. Did you hear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, wouldn't it be a good idea that whenever you ask whether the witness knows something, whether he knew it at the time or whether he learned later about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it might create some confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I entirely take the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you were following his evidence in the Milosevic case, Mr. Markovic, did you hear him give evidence that on the 24th of March there were 400 Serb security forces in the little village of Dubrave? Did you hear him give that evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I watched the broadcast occasionally, only when I had time; I didn't watch it all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, since you were listening to the conversations of people going in and out of the police station from whenever it was you were called up, did you get a picture of how many policemen had been involved in what happened in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Let me ask you something else. I think it's right, isn't it, that you do accept - or at least you did when you were interviewed by the Prosecution a few days ago - that at the time you were called up, whether that was in March or April, special units and the VJ were already starting to arrive in the area around Decane?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, please, the sort of strength of numbers that you saw arriving at the time that you were called up?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What did you mean when you told the Prosecution special units were arriving at the time you were called up?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: A tank unit, guns, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You weren't referring to paramilitary police units, Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no paramilitary police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll come back to that in a few moments. So one thing we can be clear of is that the Yugoslav Army was arriving at the time you were called up, because that's what you've just told us. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately a day or two later, but that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, I may have misunderstood you, but a few lines ago I thought you told me that at the time that the roads were blocked off, there were only 15 policemen in Decane. Is that still your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But then you told us a little earlier that the roads were blocked off a few days after you were called up. Were the Yugoslav Army there with their special units when the roads were blocked off?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you confirm, please, that throughout the war during 1998 and 1999, you personally never saw a single KLA member in uniform?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Not in full uniform, but in pieces of uniform; part of it was military, part civilian. But I never saw a full uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you from your statement page 5, paragraph 4, and see if that jogs your memory. You said: "I never saw any UCK member in uniform, even in 1999, until we left Kosovo. All of them wore civilian clothes and they were not acting like an army." Does that accurately reflect your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I just amended it by saying that sometimes I saw them wearing a combination of uniform and civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The VJ, though, that you saw arriving at the time that you were called up, they were acting like an army, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to ask you this on that topic: Internationals in the area report that VJ vehicles were being painted blue to make them look like police vehicles, but that one could see the green paint underneath to try and pretend what was going on was policing rather than military action. Did you see that, vehicles of the VJ which had been painted blue?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When, if we can just get some clarity about the roads being cut off -- have I got the position correctly, and I'm going from your statement now, the impression that you give is that the Serb civilians inside Decane were effectively stranded for a period of time. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Effectively cut off from the outside world for a short while?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was that before or after the 24th of March, the Gllogjan incident, I should say. Was it before or after the day when Otovic was killed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It was after my withdrawal from the Streoc post office and my arrival in Decani. I don't know about the incident at Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you then as somebody who was on such good terms with the Albanians in the area where you were working in the post office, were you aware of what had happened in Drenica, that is in Likoshan and Prekaze on the 28th of February and the 5th of March? I see you're furrowing your brow. Did you know what had happened?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That is quite far from Decani. No, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You hadn't heard or read in the papers that 80 Albanians, including women, a pregnant woman, the elderly, and a number of children had been shot by the police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is this the first time you've ever heard of what happened in Prekaze?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that really the truth, Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the attack on Adem Jashari's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, so you know where Adem Jashari lives, don't you? Or where he lived before he and his family were wiped out? You knew where they lived?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you hear about the attack on Adem Jashari's family, at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I don't remember. I did hear something about that, but I don't know what exactly or when. I am familiar with the incident, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that 80 Albanians were killed over a period of seven days when the police moved into those villages?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd heard of people being killed, but I wasn't familiar with the exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, earlier Mr. Emmerson did put a question to you about whether you heard about the -- let me read it. What had happened in Drenica, that is in Likoshan and Prekaze on the 28th of February and the 5th of March. And you said: "That's quite far from Decani, no, I do not know." Whereas a couple of lines further down where Mr. Emmerson asked you whether it's really the truth that this is the first time you hear of what happened in Prekaze, then your answer is: "You mean the attack on Adem Jashari's house?" So it gives the impression, since you come up with this name spontaneously, that you knew something of what happened in Prekaze, of what you earlier said, That's far from Decani, no, I do not know. It seems like you did know something about it, and even if you would not have known about details you should have told us at that time, No details had been mentioned yet, that you were aware or that you'd heard about what happened or that there was an attack on Adem Jashari's house. Because you first denied any knowledge, whereas a few lines later it turns out that at least you have a spontaneous recollection of the name of the man whose house was attacked. Or have I misunderstood you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everybody knew about the attack on Adem Jashari's house, but I thought the question was in reference to something special. I thought he was asking something specific about -- but I have no reason to conceal any knowledge of that or any other incident. I am familiar with the incident involving Adem Jashari's house, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, then your answer to that first question should have been, Are you asking for something specific or are you asking about what we all knew, that is the attack on Adem Jashari's house. That would have been the correct answer. If you are unclear about whether any specific matter or any general knowledge is asked for, please ask for clarification. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What I'm exploring with you, Mr. Markovic, is what might have been the reasons why people wanted to block access into the villages on the east side of the main road, you see. Now, you've told us everybody knows about what happened in the Jashari incident. Perhaps we can go back to the questions I asked you a minute ago. Were you aware - leaving aside numbers for a moment - that the victims included women, a pregnant woman, the elderly, and a number of young children shot in cold blood. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I knew that some people had been killed, but I didn't know about any pregnant women.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know there were children and the elderly amongst the victims?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd heard stories about children being among the victims, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you know that people had been taken out under arrest and simply lined up and put to death by the police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It must have been a matter of great concern to you as a police officer to hear that children were among the victims of police actions, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody likes it when a child gets killed, do they.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was there discussion amongst the police at Decane about making sure nothing like that ever happens again?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't with the reserve police at that time. I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Now, you told us -- I'm sorry, you said in your witness statement, Mr. Markovic, that there came a time when the roadblocks were removed. And I just want to be clear, you also at another point in your statement described it as a point in time at which the terrorists escaped. Can you tell us, please, when and how the Serb forces regained complete control of Decane?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: One could travel to Decani. There was a certain area through which one could pass, and then the police and the military arrived, and this area became ever larger. I'm not familiar with the exact date when Decani was taken over or regained.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put something to you and ask you to comment on it, all right, about whether it's accurate or not. All right. In another case which is going on in this building at the moment, the Prosecution allege that at around Easter, that is roughly mid-April, a VJ tank unit attacked Decane. Is that correct? Do you remember there being fighting with a VJ tank unit attacking Decane around Easter time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there fighting in Decane at all in the first half of 1998? Any shooting inside the town or shelling?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No fighting. There was firing on Decani from outside. A police officer named Slavko Tomasevic was wounded. I think there was shelling, too, but I can't remember exactly whether it was in 1998 or 1999. Two shells landed just next to the petrol station in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware at any time during the first half of 1998 of the VJ launching a military attack on the Albanian population of Decane?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to pick up the evidence that you've given us about the VJ units that arrived at around the time that you were called up. I mentioned earlier to you the British military attache to Belgrade. I simply want to put this to you: The records that have been filed by that individual for the period around the 24th of March record that there were VJ artillery units around Decane defended by the JSO. Now, let me ask you, first of all, do you know what those letters, JSO, stand for?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Special operations unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They are the special forces of the Serbian State Security Service, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And their commander, I suggest, is an individual whose name will be well-known to you called Franko Simatovic, otherwise known as Frenki. Is that a name you've heard?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this unit was known colloquially as "Frenki's boys," wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They'd previously been known as the "Red Berets" when they were involved in the conflict in Croatia and Bosnia, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd heard about that on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You know that Frenki Simatovic is indicted in this Tribunal for war crimes committed with that unit in Bosnia and Croatia, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd heard of that, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The JSO were stationed just outside Decane, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where were they stationed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: In this holiday resort for children.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The one that Stanisa Radosevic worked at as a security guard? Is that the one?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Try for us, please, Mr. Markovic. When did they arrive, before or after you were called up?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Going back to all the information you hear about -- from police officers of senior rank wandering in and out of the police station, did you hear anything about the tactics and techniques that the JSO used to use on Albanian villages or not?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I ask for clarification on one of your questions? You said the records that have been filed by that individual, for the period around the 24th of March, record there were VJ artillery units around Decani defended by the JSO. Is that Decani was defended by the JSO against VJ artillery units, or I might not have fully grabbed --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, the suggestion is that the JSO were guarding and defending the VJ artillery units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it's clear to me. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And I think it's clear also, isn't it, Your Honours, from the answer the witness gave to the proposition put by Mr. Emmerson that this was happening at least by 24 March.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know if it is clear at all. Mr. Di Fazio is more than welcome to re-examine on it, if he wants to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, I want to put to you that the JSO had a base next to Decane monastery. Would that be the same -- roughly the same area as where you're describing this camp?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me ask you a little bit about other deployments that you are aware of. The VJ, and in particular the 549th Motorised Brigade under Bozidar Delic, you knew, didn't you, that they were stationed on three large hills immediately adjacent to Lake Radoniq?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you saying that you know that they weren't, or you don't know one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to suggest to you, you could hear the shelling coming from Donji Bites?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that one could, actually. It's a large distance separating Radonjic Lake and Decani, about 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, let me put it to you this way: Since you followed General Delic's evidence in the Milosevic case, were you watching at the point in which he told the Tribunal that he had forces stationed on those three hills from April 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're certainly not in a position to suggest, are you, that there were not Serb forces in the area around the lake throughout 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What about the military police battalion, because they were deployed there as well, I suggest, in the area of the lake? Are you aware about them, or is that also outside your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I know nothing at all about the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the deployment of the JSO when they took part in operations at all?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you, presumably, can't tell us one way or the other whether the JSO were conducting operations to the east of the Peje-Pristina road during 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me ask you a little bit about your own involvement, Mr. Markovic, and in particular let's ask you, if I may, about some of the answers you've given about your visit to Dashinoc or Dasinovac when the bodies of Slobodan Radosevic and Milos Radunovic were found. Now, we have heard evidence from Stanisa Radosevic and also from (redacted), that the Albanian houses in Dasinovac had been burnt down by the time those bodies were discovered. Can you tell us, please, when you first went to Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It was then, when we found the bodies, Slobo and Milos.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How long after the Serb troops had entered the area were you on the scene?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know when the Serb troops entered. We just went of our own accord and unaccompanied.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us, in the evidence you gave in answer to Mr. Di Fazio, that you went in a Pinzgauer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you said: "We were all uniformed because there was still shooting going on." This is page 36, line 7. Was there still shooting going on around the area of Dasinovac when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sporadically.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you could hear that, could you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So tell us, please, were the Albanian houses burnt down?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see from where I stood, and I didn't go that far into the village. The first house near the spot where we were is at a distance of about 300 metres, and that is Marko Vukicevic's house. There's plenty of houses once you get past that one, but it was impossible to see from our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you see smoke rising from the haystacks?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I wasn't paying attention to that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which route did your Pinzgauer take to get to Dashinoc/Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The Ljubarda road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So Lubarda to where, Pozhare?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Pozar, the canal, Ljubarda and on to Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And along the way, Mr. Markovic, did you see houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Houses on fire, I don't remember. There were houses that were burned to the ground, but I'm not sure if any were actually ablaze as we were passing. Well, the first thing -- the first thing that needs to be said is that there weren't that many houses lining that road to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just tell us about the houses that you saw that had been burnt to the ground. Where were they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: The Decani-Luka-Pozar road, although there aren't that many houses there. In Pozar, over Kordolija way, there are several houses, and on the left-hand side of the road a handful of houses. Other than that, there are maybe two or three houses lining that road, so there weren't that many to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Leaving aside the houses you yourself saw, did you hear, either then or afterwards, from other police officers about the number of Albanian houses that had been put to the torch?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I never asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Isn't that something that would be a matter of concern to you, Mr. Markovic, as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know who burnt those houses down?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would it be a matter of concern to you if you knew it was the police? Would that bother you as a police officer, Albanian houses being burnt down?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, that would be an unpleasant thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it would be unforgivable, wouldn't it? Wouldn't it be unforgivable?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, I want to suggest that you know full well who was involved, Mr. Markovic, because you took part in the looting of houses and the setting of them on fire in Dasinovac. And may I make it clear, I'm not intending to tell you something amusing. I suggest to you that you took part?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: You are just not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see Stanisa Radosevic in the area around Dasinovac, when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, since you've told us that you saw him frequently in Decane and discussed things with him, did you discuss the fact that you had been there, when his father's body was discovered, with him?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you tell him about that and did he tell you that he'd been to Dasinovac, as well, around that time?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember him telling me about him being -- having been in Dasinovac around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see earlier on when I asked when it was that Stanisa Radosevic was called up to the reserve police, you told us that the only thing I can be sure of is that he had been called up by the time those bodies were found in Dashinoc. What was it that made you so sure, that by then, he was in the police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that he was there. Why? I don't know. It's just something that is etched in my memory, him being in the police at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, try and help us, why is that etched in your memory, if he wasn't there and he never told you -- MR. DI FAZIO: He said he doesn't know. You can read it: "Why? I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm in Your Honours' hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you first clarify what exactly is etched in his memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What is it that's etched in your memory, Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: You asked me if I could remember, with any degree of certainty, when Stanisa was in the police. I responded after I thought it out well, that approximately at the time when his father was found, he was in the police, but -- and that is what is etched in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you saw him about that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Decani is a small place, willy-nilly, you have to bump into people. It just has one street so you have to meet people.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where was he serving his police service?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think in Decani. Should be Decani. I'm not 100 per cent sure. Should be Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You know him well, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Pretty well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're good friends?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I have to say it to you again. There are 700 Serbs in Decani. Everybody knows everything about everyone, so it's impossible not to know people.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you think of any reason why he should tell the Tribunal he was never in the police or the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's because you and he were together with Novak, Miloica, and Miloica Vlahovic and Goran Vlahovic and Novak Stijovic and Momo Stijovic, looting and burning the houses in the village that your parents had come from, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I wasn't with him, and I don't know that they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going on to another topic now. I wonder if that would be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've got about 20 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So where you earlier indicated that one and a half hour would do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry it's taking slightly longer but I hope it's not unhelpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've got 20 minutes left then still, Mr. Di Fazio, that remains, then if he -- would you have any questions in re-examination? MR. DI FAZIO: I think I might but they'll be very brief, and I'll be in a better position in the next half-hour to know. But they'll will be brief, all or no questions at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Will there be any questions by other Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very few, if any.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Emmerson is covering all of the ground that I would have wished to cover with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The reason I'm asking is that, of course, the next witness -- there might be some time remaining, and I have to tell you another thing, that tomorrow we'll start half an hour later than usual, which means that we have not the full time tomorrow, either. Therefore ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt, just on the question of timing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Assuming we take something approximating to our normal break, the amount of time that would be left over today would be relatively limited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do think it's likely that, subject to the views of other Defence counsel, that the next witness's evidence-in-chief could be taken really quite shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so it may be that without trying to put him into the witness box this afternoon, the time could be saved by taking him more quickly tomorrow morning -- or tomorrow afternoon because, as I say, I doubt that his evidence-in-chief or, indeed, his cross-examination will need to take a great deal of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I'm -- the Chamber is a bit hesitant to just give up a half an hour if that still remains. What the Chamber will do during the break, we'll inquire with the Victims and Witnesses Section about the condition of the witness, and we do not exclude for the possibility that we would continue once we've finished with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break until ten minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic, I want to ask you some questions about what happened when you went to the canal area during the period of time when bodies were being removed from the canal. In your witness statement, you say that by the time you arrived at the Lake Radonjic canal, there were what you describe as active policemen and crime experts already on the scene. Do you know the date that you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know how long the operation in the canal area had been going on by the time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Had some bodies already been removed by the time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you don't think any bodies had been removed by the time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that they were removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Were the press there when you got there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there were any international observers there when you arrived or whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you at the canal before or after the recovery of the bodies in Dashinoc -- Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're sure about that, are you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't understand that answer. Are you sure that you went to the canal after you were at Dasinovac, or were you at the canal before you went to Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it was after Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you went to Dasinovac, were you aware that there was an operation already going on at the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: One of the international observers who went to the canal on about the 9th of September said that as he approached the lake from the direction of Prilep, he could see that many houses in that area, too, had been burned down and that haystacks were still on fire. Again, can you help us with that, please, from your recollection? Did you see houses and haystacks on fire in the area around the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Prilep is very far from canal. I didn't pass through Prilep, so I can't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see any Serb forces engaged in operations whilst you were driving to the canal; in other words, en route to the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How many days did you go to the canal, one day or more than one?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I've been there only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you say there were active policemen there. What do you mean by active policemen?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I am a reserve policeman and they were active-duty policemen. They were fully employed in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This was the end of summer. As far as you can recall, what was the weather like whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't cold. It was the usual summer weather, not too hot. It wasn't cloudy, just the usual type of weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There wasn't any heavy rainfall whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you knew, didn't you, that there'd been a major Serb offensive in this area immediately before this?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Markovic, you knew, didn't you, that the Serb forces had taken control of Gllogjan and Irzniq and all of those villages immediately before this operation took place?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why did you think it was safe for police to travel there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: If somebody tells you you can go there, it's safe, and if that person is from the police station, I presumed that it was okay for us to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you had no idea -- so that we're clear, you had no idea that there'd been fighting in the area between the Serb forces and the KLA around Gllogjan and Irzniq in the villages in that vicinity in the days and weeks before you went to the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the time. I heard later that there was fighting, but not then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you did find out later on that there had been fighting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How long after you went to Dasinovac did you go to the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't a long period. Approximately a week, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, now with the greatest respect, Mr. Markovic, that simply cannot be right. On the records that we have from the recovery operation. If you're right in saying that you were at the canal after Dasinovac, it must have been the next day or within a day or two. Do you think it might have been within a day or two?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I can agree with you, but I cannot give you a specific time-period. It may have been two days, it may have been a week. I know that these two incidents were close to one another, but I cannot say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because when you were in Dasinovac you told us you heard the sound of gun-fire, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said that I heard intermittent gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you knew there was fighting going on at the time you were in Dasinovac, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what we heard, then, didn't indicate any heavy fighting; it was just sporadic fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, again, we can listen to this on another occasion, but on the videotape of the canal whilst the recovery operation is going on, it's possible to hear the sound of gun-fire. Now, were you aware of gun-fire whilst you were at the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand you. You mean at that particular moment or before that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you were at the canal on the only day you've told us you went there, did you hear gun-fire whilst you were at the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you, you told us that you learnt afterwards that there had been fighting in the area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this: Do you know generally, leaving this incident aside for the moment, do you know generally what the Serb paramilitary forces did with the bodies of civilians that they had killed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You don't know how they disposed of them?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware of a practice of trying to hide the bodies of Albanian civilians -- MR. DI FAZIO: Third time. Third time, if Your Honours please. "Do you know generally what the" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, overruled. Mr. Emmerson, of course we are not seeking five or six times but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, no, it's a different question about a specific practice now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware of a practice amongst the paramilitaries of trying to hide the bodies of Albanian civilians who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Presumably by now, though, you're aware, aren't you, from the media, if from nowhere else, that large numbers of bodies of Albanian civilians, including civilians killed in western Kosovo, were shipped to Serbia and hidden there.
