You know about that, don't you? They're still being repatriated to Kosovo, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about it in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Bodies of people that were put into containers and hidden in the Danube. Have you heard about that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I only heard about that in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And buried in a mass grave in Serbia and now being repatriated to Albania, you heard about that, too, in Batajnica?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you know that they were included --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm asking myself what the relevance of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm just moving on to that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know whether anybody had been killed or did you find out whether anybody had been killed by the Serb forces during the September offensive that you've told us that you learned about?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: There were stories circulating around, but nothing concrete. And there were stories that people got killed in the -- during shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you hear any stories about what was done with their bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever visit the economic farm whilst you were conducting this operation, whilst you were present in the canal area? The nearby economic farm, did you yourself go there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this - and please be very careful with your answer - when you arrived at the canal scene or at any time whilst you were there, did you see fully fleshed bodies floating in the water in the concrete section of the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing bodies floating in the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that I'm clear, I'm talking about the concrete section of the canal, not the ravine lower down, but the concrete section of the canal. I'm suggesting to you that there were fully fleshed, recent bodies in the water in the concrete section of the canal. Did you see those?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us already that, as far as you know, no bodies had been removed from the site. That's still correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Madam Usher, I wonder if I could ask you to hand the witness, the Judges, and the Prosecution a copy of this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that still needs a number, I take it? It will be uploaded soon on the e-court, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D31, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I think it should be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a photograph, Mr. Markovic, taken from a set of photographs that were apparently taken during the recovery operation. Do you see those two bodies floating in the water there? Again, I ask you, having seen the photograph, did you ever see those two bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, because, Mr. Markovic, those two bodies didn't show up on any of the post-mortem reports; they simply disappeared, unaccounted for. Can you help us with that at all, as to why bodies so recently killed might have disappeared? Anything you saw that could help us with that?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about it. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where were the victims of Serb paramilitaries being disposed of in this area, Mr. Markovic?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you took bodies out of the area, where did you remove bodies from?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: We loaded them on a vehicle, and they were driven away to Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where did you remove them from exactly? Where did you take them from?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: From the place where the concrete part of the canal ends and where the part which is not covered with concrete begins.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if I can use this expression, down in the canyon section is where you were removing bodies from?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there ever a time when the bodies of men and women were laid out in separate lines at the canal area?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you about these Roma that you've told us about? What was their function?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean specifically in relation to the canal?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let's start with that. What was their function in relation to the canal?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: They helped with collecting -- with the collecting of bodies from the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were they police officers?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there any particular reason why Roma civilians were being used for this job?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware of either those Roma civilians or other Roma civilians being used by the police for other jobs?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, just so we're clear, does that mean you're not aware of any other occasion on which Roma civilians have been used by the police?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be a translation problem. I'd just like a clear answer to the question, if I can, please. Yes or no, do you know of any other occasion on which Roma civilians have been used by the police in any form of investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Markovic, you'll now be further cross-examined by Mr. Guy-Smith, who is counsel for Mr. Balaj. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you were removing bodies from the canal section of the -- I believe you called it the canyon section of the canal, did you see a car in that area?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: There was a vehicle. There were police cars; I think there was an ambulance as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm referring to a car that was actually in the canyon section itself where you were recovering bodies from, an overturned car.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: It may have been there. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have no memory of that. How much time did you spend down in the canyon section removing bodies, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: About three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you were down in the canyon section for that three- to four-hour period of time, were you walking about the area directly below where the concrete part of the canal ends?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you're telling us, as you sit here, that you do not recall seeing an overturned car in that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I wasn't paying attention. I don't rule out the possibility that it may have been there, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing any individuals attempting to pry the car, any large object in that part of the canyon, up from the canyon bottom with large pieces of wood?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have nothing for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: At the canal, did you see any paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see any containers?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "containers."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Any containers that might be used to ship goods, materials.

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see any fresh corpses on the banks of the canal or the banks of the canyon?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You were answering questions by Mr. Emmerson in which you described that there was some special forces units guarding VJ artillery units. Have you got any idea about when that occurred; namely, that you saw -- namely, that you were aware of the special forces, I think it was JSO, guarding VJ artillery units?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before the witness answers, there were two separate parts of the passage which I think Mr. Di Fazio is conflating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, could you please specifically refer to the answers the witness gave in this respect and guide us to the relevant places. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Page 76, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, just ... MR. DI FAZIO: The witness was asked if he knew what JSO stood for, he agreed that they are special operations units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And asked questions about Frenki.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And then he was asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I'm -- MR. DI FAZIO: That --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- mainly seeking his answers because you were referring -- you were asking questions that there was special force. Have you got any idea --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I may be able to help. There were two separate lines of questioning; one was about the special forces guarding the VJ units, and the other one appears on page 78, line 11, in which the witness confirmed that the JSO had a base next to the Decane monastery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because if you want to put to the witness that he confirmed that these special forces were guarding the VJ artillery, I could not find that in the answers of the witness, but if you would guide me to the place where he confirmed that in his answers. I see the question, the question appears 76 -- 76, line -- well, let's say 8, 9 approximately, and the only question was: What does JSO stand for? But I do not see any confirmation at this moment about -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what was part of the question. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Emmerson's question: "The records that have been filed by that individual for the period around the 24th of March record that there were VJ artillery units around Decani defended by JSO" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was the question, not an answer. I do not find any confirmation of the witness at this moment on this matter. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, I think it might be helpful to Mr. Di Fazio to look at page 78, line 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There I find confirmation but not of exactly the same thing. MR. DI FAZIO: Obviously, Mr. Emmerson was taking the witness to that point, and we didn't get to the point of getting a clear answer, and that's why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then what you did, Mr. Di Fazio, you referred to the answers the witness gave, and the answers do not say anything -- of course, you could elicit answers from him in which you, as a matter, seek further confirmation of what actually was not specifically asked by Mr. Emmerson at the time. But I'm just rather precise in references to -- MR. DI FAZIO: No, no, I think Your Honour may be -- obviously, Your Honour is correct and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I do not mind if you want to -- MR. DI FAZIO: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- further elicit any information as far as this is concerned. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Perhaps I'll just revert back to a simple and more direct questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did the JSO guard VJ artillery units, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. You were asked about their presence in the area. Were they present in your area at the same time that VJ artillery units were present?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And can you give the Trial Chamber a time on when that might have occurred, when those special -- the JSO and VJ artillery units were in the area simultaneously?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I think in May, late April/May, thereabouts. That's at least what I was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I've got no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I have one question that still puzzles me a bit. You may have understood from Mr. Emmerson's questions that he tried to understand why you were so sure about -- at least -- what's his name --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Stanisevic [sic] to be with you in the police at the moment, certainly not later than the moment when you recovered the body of his father. Are you certain that you did not go with him to the place where his father's body was recovered or later go there together with him? Are you sure that he didn't tell you about going there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that he wasn't with me then, and I'm sure that I didn't go there with him. We did talk about the place where his father's body was found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you also sure that he didn't tell you that he went there?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure. I'm sure we didn't discuss that specifically or that he was later there. I certainly don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in view of there being disagreement on when he came to the police force, when he became a police officer, are you certain that he did not -- he was not in any way involved in the operation you described later, that is, at the Lake Radonjic canal area?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know if he was there or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You consider it a possibility?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was with the police, wasn't he? So it was possible, but he was a reserve policeman; and in the light of that fact, I don't think he would have been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you were a reserve policeman, as well?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why would it be surprising that he, as a reserve police officer, would not be there, whereas you, being a reserve police officer, as well, that you were present?

utterances.speaker: ZVONKO MARKOVIC
utterances.text: I was just guarding the scene. I wasn't part of the actual operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. This concludes your testimony, on the assumption that there's -- it has not triggered the need for further questions. This concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you for having come to The Hague and having answered questions of parties and of the Bench. May I ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom, Mr. Markovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the extent it was not clear yet, the exhibit, I think it was -- let me just have a look. P39 is, because that's not clear on the record, is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P39 is the video --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We discussed it, but there was no clear decision that it was admitted into evidence, and there was no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would like to tender the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that would be, Madam Registrar, we have -- the number was already given, that's D -- D31. Any objection? MR. DI FAZIO: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's admitted into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, as far as the passage I put to this witness from his brother's witness statement is concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I've asked Mr. Di Fazio to consider the position. Either the witness statement could be exhibited and admitted, or Mr. Di Fazio can make a stipulation that the passage I put to the witness appears in the witness statement under that witness's signature of the relevant date. So may we -- may we consider that position overnight and we can revert to Your Honours tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were three other exhibits that Your Honour left us to respond to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was -- I think it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: P30, D30, and the Andjelkovic notebooks, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson, I am aware that this is a pending issue. Neither of them are urgent.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment, we have ten minutes left. Now we can do two things; send the witness away, which is not a very elegant way of dealing with the witness, or to invite him in, to ask him to make a solemn declaration, and that we start at least a couple of minutes, and we explain to him that we are -- I think that is the best way of dealing with it. So, therefore, Madam Usher, would you please escort the next witness into the courtroom. And any protective measures, Mr. Di Fazio? No protective measures? MR. DI FAZIO: Just one point at which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- I'll be going into -- seeking to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And your next witness would be? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I'll call Momcilo Antic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Momcilo Antic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Antic. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Antic, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. The text will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Antic. Mr. Antic, I would, first of all, like to apologise that you had to wait for such a long time this afternoon. The Chamber is aware that you had a -- that you have a journey behind you which -- well, you might be even a bit exhausted by it. So therefore, we expected, as a matter of fact, that we would have a little bit more time for you this afternoon. We'll start now with your examination, but it will not take very long. It will take a very limited period of time, and then we'll continue tomorrow. But at least now -- now you've seen the courtroom and -- otherwise, you might be worried about what it looks like to be in this courtroom. So we'll make a start, not longer than ten minutes, and then we'll continue tomorrow. You'll first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, I would like you to first provide the Trial Chamber with a picture of yourself, and to that end I would like some personal details, please. Give us -- or, rather, let me ask you to confirm this. Your full name is Momcilo Antic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You're going to have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I heard the witness, but perhaps the witness should come a bit closer to the microphone because otherwise the interpreters cannot hear you. So would you speak a little bit more into the microphones. I take it that you affirmed that you are Momcilo Antic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And you have a nickname, Momo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You were born on the 12th of July, 1962?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And you are Serbian and lived most of your life in Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In fact, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: In [indiscernible] and I lived in the village of Locane.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long had you lived in the village of Locane prior to 1998?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: For 27 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And with whom did you live in Locane?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: With my family, my wife, two sons, my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd like you to provide the Trial Chamber with a snap-shot of your domestic situation in very early 1998. Which village were you living in? Who was in the house living with you? And what was your occupation at that time?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: I lived in Locane with my two sons, my wife, and my father. My cousins were also there, my aunt, my neighbours, and my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'll ask you about that, the broader situation. But as far as your actual house was concerned, do I take it that you lived in the house with your father, your two sons, and your wife; or did that also include your cousins and aunt in the same -- in the same building?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. They had their own house and I had mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So who was actually living in your own house? Who was actually in the building under that roof?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: In my house?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In your house, yes.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: My father, myself, my wife, and our two sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was your occupation again, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: I worked in a factory in Istinic, a pump factory; they produced pumps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long had you been working in that factory in Istinic prior to 1998?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: For eight years. After that, I worked with the reserve police forces, the Decani SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'd just like -- perhaps we can clarify this business of the reserve police. When did you actually start working with the reserve police as a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: I started in 1990, and I continued working until the very last day when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were in the reserve policemen -- in the reserve police as a full-time reserve policeman? That was your day-to-day work?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: I worked whenever it was necessary, not full time, not every day. I would do five- or six-month stints, and then I would be on leave for a month or so, that sort of pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. But in the period of time leading up to 1998, were you actually going to the factory in Istinic and working there?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: No, not in 1998. In 1998, I was with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. So by the time 1998 came around, you were no longer going to work in the factory, and each day you would be carrying out policeman's duties as a reserve policeman. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO ANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, in 1998 throughout, until I was wounded. And later, I was at the military academy hospital in Belgrade, and I was no longer able to carry out my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I think that's probably as good a time as any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Antic, as I told you before, it would be only very short today. We'll continue tomorrow at a quarter to 3.00, and then we'll be in another courtroom, that would be Courtroom I, but they'll bring you at the right place. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Antic out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back, Mr. Antic. But I would first like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony, although limited, you have given and the testimony still to be given. Madam Usher. I'd like to go into private session for just one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 4th day of April, 2007, at 2.45 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.03 p.m.,
